chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not befitting for anyone to enter into Ihram before the designated Mawaqit (stations) which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had fixed, except if he fears missing the month regarding the Umrah.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فَوْتَ الشَّهْر: Missing or losing the month (of the season)
key_terms.مَوَاقِيت: Designated stations or places where pilgrims enter Ihram

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to enter Ihram before the designated Mawaqit?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the standard legal principle that Ihram must commence at the designated Mawaqit, reinforcing the Prophetic tradition of structured pilgrimage rites. It introduces a specific juristic exception for Umrah, where fear of missing the sacred month permits entering Ihram earlier, highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual precision with practical necessity to ensure the validity of the act.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘It is not befitting for anyone that he should wear Ihraam beside the junctures which Rasool-Allahsaww had designated, except if he fears losing the month regarding the Umra’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Mu‘awiyah who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say this Hadith.

‘It is not proper to assume the state of Ihram before Miqat. They are (places for assuming the state of Ihram) designated by the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, except when one is afraid of missing the month of al-‘Umrah.’”
